craft_notes: Sthāyin: well-over-pit (the vertigo instrument: standing between the two — L3's reading kept, never inverted). Rows: row 2 (undivided→dissolving plainly). Close: plainly (niścaya — the certainty-adverb: the DISSOLVING is certain, not the anxiety). Rejected: 'black hole' — killed: well-and-pit kept (both water-words: vṛṣṭi-vṛṣṭi? no — setu/bhīma keep their own degrees: great-pit); 'kundalini drop' — killed: dissolving kept (laya, no ascent implied).

lines: Above well and great pit, standing, from looking:
undivided mind rightly — mind dissolving plainly.
l4.sanskrit_cite: kūpādike mahāgarte sthitvopari nirīkṣaṇāt | avikalpamateḥ samyak sadyas cittalayaḥ sphuṭam

reads_against.argmap: What dissolves from above the pit? → Looking down from above the pit dissolves mind plainly.
c1_essence: Above pit, undivided mind: dissolving plainly.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vīra (stillness reached through force of attention)
